Latin word

ita

adverb

so, in such a way, to such a degree; so, thus, in such a way; yes (it is so)

In this lexicon

  • so

    also used · classical · Traupman 382

  • thus

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 7.8.4: factum est ita (Lewis & Short); Ter. And. 192: Ita ajunt (“so they say”)

  • yes

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. And. 849b–850: Mihine? — Ita.; Hor. S. 2.7.2: Dāvusne? — ita, Dāvus; Traupman 250: ita and sīc mean “it is so”; Traupman 250, 410

  • sī ita est: case

    classical

  • haud ita prīdem (nōn ita prīdem): long ago

    classical

  • Haud ita est.: that’s not so

    classical

  • Quid ita nōn?: why not?

    classical
